useCase.name: Show who is waiting, send the child, and record that they left and when — the only record of a child leaving during the day
useCase.featureRef: 29.7 Working the pickup queue and releasing a child

steps.note: One step. The API decides whether the collection is early, against the configured end of the day; an early one without a reason is refused (BR-8).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. An early collection with no reason, a request already completed, no open request, or one not yet sent to the gate completes nothing. Where the attendance mark cannot be made, the release still stands.
plan.atomicity: One write: the request completed and the collection record — the child, the time and the branch (BR-4, BR-6). An early collection also marks that day's attendance as an early departure (BR-8). **No collector is recorded**, and nothing is ever deleted (BR-11).

operations.name: pickup.request.complete

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No open pickup request for this child — every release is against one (E8).

errors.meaning: The collection is early and no reason was given.
The request has already been completed.
errors.notWritten: It cannot be completed again — the child was released at the time recorded.

errors.meaning: The attendance for that day could not be marked as an early departure.
errors.notWritten: The attendance mark, which needs correcting.
errors.note: Reported, rather than the day standing as a full day present.

errors.meaning: There is no open pickup request for this child.
errors.notWritten: Nothing is released — every release is against a request.

errors.meaning: The request has not been sent to the gate.
errors.note: The lifecycle completes a request only once it is sent to the gate, or after a refusal. The use case writes no exception for completing one straight from the queue.

planningRules.rule: Never record who collected. There is no field for it and no list to check against — a name written here would be a guess in the one record an incident is investigated from (BR-4, E1, AC-4).
Where the staff member voices any doubt about the person, do not complete — refuse the release and call the School Admin. The system cannot refuse on its own, so the judgement is theirs (BR-5, A1).
Never supply the time. It is when the child was handed over, as the staff member says (BR-6).
Never write the early-collection reason. Ask for it where the collection is early — without it nothing is completed, and the day would otherwise read as a full day present (BR-8, E2, AC-9).
Report an attendance mark that failed. The child is released regardless, and the mark then needs correcting through the attendance correction, not here (E4).
A refused request is completed only once the School Admin has settled it — and nothing records what the School Admin decided. Say so (OQ-3).
staff_id and branch_id come from $session.

reversal.statement: A completed request is final, and the collection record is never deleted — it is the only record that the child left (BR-11, E9). A wrong attendance mark is corrected through the attendance correction.

request.text: Ayesha ko 1:52 pe hand over kar diya

resolvedPlans.context: Security, Johar Town. Ayesha's request sent to the gate. The normal end of the day is 13:30.
resolvedPlans.outcome: Completed at 13:52, and the day stands as a full day. No collector is recorded, because there is none to record.

request.text: Hamza 11 baje apne abbu ke saath chala gaya

resolvedPlans.context: Security, Johar Town. Hamza's request sent to the gate. The normal end of the day is 13:30.
resolvedPlans.outcome: Asks for the reason first — the collection is early. Then completed at 11:00, with that day's attendance marked as an early departure. "With his father" is not recorded: there is no field for who collected, and the staff member's word for it is not a check.

parameters.name: request_id

errors.meaning: The child has already been released against this request.

planningRules.rule: Refuse whenever the staff member has any doubt. The system holds no list of who may collect and cannot refuse on its own, so the judgement rests with whoever is on duty — and a planner never talks them out of it (BR-5, AC-6).
Never write the note. It is their account, and it is what is read if the collection is ever questioned (BR-5, BR-10).
Tell them to call the School Admin themselves. The use case says the School Admin is called and describes no message that does it (BR-5, A1).
Say that what happens next is not specified. Nothing records the outcome of the School Admin's call (OQ-3).
staff_id and branch_id come from $session.

reversal.statement: Once the School Admin has settled it, the child is released against the same request and it is completed. The refusal and its note stay on the record (BR-11).
